name: minesweeper
title: Minesweeper
description: The mine-clearing game in the panel, keyboard only: the arrows move, Enter opens, F or / flags, N starts over. The board, the clock and the best times persist.
author: pal

settings.label: Difficulty
settings.description: The board's size and mines. Applies to the next board, at once when nothing is open yet; a game in progress plays out first.

store.tagline: Minesweeper in the panel, one hand on the arrows
features: The board as a view level: the title carries the mines left, the header the mine counter, the clock and the best time, `cmd+k` lists every move
One-handed: the arrows move the cursor, `Enter` opens, `/` (just above the arrows) flags; `hjkl`, `F` and `Space` do the same
The classic rules: the first open is always safe and opens an area, an empty cell floods open, `Enter` on a number whose flags are placed opens around it
Beginner 9 by 9, intermediate 16 by 16, expert 30 by 16 (a setting); a best time and a won count per level
An open ripples out from the cell, a lost game's mines ripple out from the one that went off; the numbers wear the classic colours on the panel's own hues
The clock runs from the first open and only while the board is on screen; Escape leaves at any point and the game is there when you come back, across restarts

screenshots.caption: Mid-game on beginner: the mine counter, the clock and the best time above the board, the keys under it
Cleared: the mines left are flagged, the time, a new best
A mine went off: every mine shows, a wrong flag is crossed out
Expert, 30 by 16 with 99 mines, fits the panel

actions.title: Open
actions.description: On a number whose flags are all placed, opens the cells around it (Open around).

actions.title: New game
actions.description: A fresh board at the difficulty setting; asks first mid-game, and is Enter once the game is over.

minesweeper.description: The board. Escape leaves mid-game; the board and the clock wait for you.

keys.title: Move (also down, left, right, and hjkl)
Open; on a satisfied number, open around it; a new game once the game is over
